chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus, from Abu Wahb al-Basri, who said:

I entered Madinah and went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have come to you but I have not visited the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him).' He said, 'How terrible what you have done! If you were not from our Shia, I would not have even looked at you. Do you not visit the one whom Allah, the Exalted, visits with the angels, and the prophets visit with the believers?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I did not know this.' He said, 'Then know that the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) is superior in the sight of Allah than all of the Imams, and he has the reward of their deeds, and they are elevated according to the measure of their deeds.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Believers (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting the grave of Imam Ali (a.s.) and his rank among the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarah* underscores the cosmological significance of Imam Ali’s (a.s.) grave, portraying it as a focal point where divine, angelic, and prophetic visitation converge. It articulates the Shia doctrine of *Fadilat al-A'imma* (superiority of the Imams) by establishing that Imam Ali (a.s.) possesses the cumulative reward of all subsequent Imams, thereby serving as the spiritual source of their elevated ranks.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father and Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb both narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā Al-‘Aťťār, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān Al-Naysābūri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad Al-Yamāni, from Manī’ ibn Ḥajjāj, from Yūnus, from Abī Wahab Al-Basri, who said:

I entered Madīnah and went to Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) and said, “May I sacrifice myself for you! I have come to you but I have not gone to the Ziyārah of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.).” Imam (a.s.) replied, “How terrible! If you were not one of our Shia, I would not have even looked at you. Do you not go to the Ziyārah of the one to whose Ziyārah Allāh, the Exalted, along with His angels goes, and (the Ziyārah to which) the prophets and the believers go?!” “May I sacrifice myself for you! I did not know this,” I said. Imam (a.s.) said: Then know that the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) has a higher rank with Allāh than all of the Imams (a.s.). The Imams (a.s.) are elevated (above others) based on the number of their deeds, and the reward for their deeds is (registered) for the Commander of the Believers (a.s.).
